extracted.intended_audience: writers, artists, and students of aesthetics or philosophy interested in the theory of artistic intuition and the relations between instinct and intelligence
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply Bergson's aesthetic-philosophical principles for creative work: privileging lived intuition/sympathy over purely intellectual or external description, depicting intention and movement within life, and using language to free consciousness. Useful for writers aiming to render inner life rather than merely assembled features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instinct is sympathy / intuition as lived sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Instinct is sympathy... by intuition I mean instinct that has become disinterested, self-conscious, capable of reflecting upon its object and of enlarging it indefinitely."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat artistic intuition as a sympathetic, inward participation in the object rather than an external, intellectual observation. The artist's method is not primarily cognitive analysis but a lived entering-into the subject that reflects upon and enlarges its object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place the artist back within the object by sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: "The artist tries to regain [the intention of life], in placing himself back within the object by a kind of sympathy, in breaking down, by an effort of intuition, the barrier that space puts up between him and his model."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting characters, scenes, or organisms, aim to 'enter' them—convey their internal organization, feeling, and purposive movement—rather than listing external features. Use techniques that collapse the spatial/objective distance between observer and observed (embodied perspective, free indirect discourse, sensory immersion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict the "intention of life" (movement that binds features) rather than assembled features
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our eye perceives the features of the living being, merely as assembled, not as mutually organized. The intention of life, the simple movement that runs through the lines, that binds them together and gives them significance, escapes it. This intention is just what the artist tries to regain."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the underlying movement, rhythm, or organizing principle of a scene or character so that disparate details cohere into a living whole. Avoid treating description as a catalogue; seek the formative gesture or dynamic that unifies form and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor lived intuition over mere representation
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Ammophila... discerns it from within, quite otherwise than by a process of knowledge--by an intuition (lived rather than represented), which is probably like what we call divining sympathy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer techniques that convey immediate, embodied experience (showing, sensory detail, kinesthetic language) rather than explanatory or representational commentary. Let readers 'live' the perception rather than simply be told about it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intuition to supplement, not replace, intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: "On the one hand, it will utilize the mechanism of intelligence itself to show how intellectual molds cease to be strictly applicable; and on the other hand, by its own work, it will suggest to us the vague feeling, if nothing more, of what must take the place of intellectual molds."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine rigorous shaping (structure, form, craft) with intuitive material that resists full intellectual capture. Use structure to frame intuition but allow moments that exceed neat conceptualization—the text should both show how concepts fail and gesture toward what they miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reducing life to inert/intellectual molds
rubrics_metrics.description: "Intelligence, by means of science... will deliver up to us more and more completely the secret of physical operations; of life it brings us, and moreover only claims to bring us, a translation in terms of inertia."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware flattening living processes into mechanical or merely explanatory descriptions. In fiction and poetry, do not let analytic metaphors strip away vitality; preserve the sense of animation and reciprocal interpenetration in living beings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray consciousness through choice and potentialities
rubrics_metrics.description: "Consciousness seems proportionate to the living being's power of choice. It lights up the zone of potentialities that surrounds the act. It fills the interval between what is done and what might be done."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatize inner life by showing alternatives, hesitations, and unrealized possibilities. Show characters' fields of possible action rather than only enacted behavior—this communicates depth of consciousness and the sense of interior freedom or constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use language to free consciousness (let words grapple with other mechanisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The cerebral mechanisms that correspond to the words have this in particular, that they can be made to grapple with other mechanisms... Meanwhile consciousness... is restored and set free."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat language not merely as label but as a dynamic instrument: use phrasing, syntax, and semantic interplay to create tensions that reveal and liberate interior states. Employ metaphors and rhetorical structures that make mental mechanisms engage one another and thus produce higher awareness in the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design devices that free attention rather than trap it
rubrics_metrics.description: (Newcomen engine example) "A difference of the same kind... would be found between the brain of an animal and the human brain... the first holding the attention captive, the second setting it at liberty."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft narrative or formal techniques that allow readers' attention to be opened and deflected—enable associative play and reflection—rather than fixating them on a single mechanical procedure. Use variance, self-reflexive elements, or layers that release rather than monopolize focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evoke reciprocal interpenetration and continuous creation
rubrics_metrics.description: "By the sympathetic communication which it establishes between us and the rest of the living, by the expansion of our consciousness which it brings about, it introduces us into life's own domain, which is reciprocal interpenetration, endlessly continued creation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for works that suggest mutual permeation between subject and world—portray relations as processes of continual creation rather than as static oppositions. Use imagery and form that imply ongoing transformation and interconnectedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious of over-intellectualizing form (the more intellect, the more matter is spatialized)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The more consciousness is intellectualized, the more is matter spatialized. So that the evolutionist philosophy... has given itself in advance, ready made, the intelligence of which it claims to show the genesis."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting conceptual systems or geometric/formal schemes predefine the lived reality you intend to portray. Let perception and lived relation determine form where appropriate; do not force life into prearranged intellectual categories at the expense of nuance and immediacy.
